transcript: Anwen went north at seven on Thursday morning, the first of the fourth month, on Greywater's van. The van stood at the head of the long quay, with its horses in and its lamps lit against the grey. It was slate blue. Mace was on the box and Nairn beside him, with Ruddock and Tib and Stiles behind. And Pyke on the tailboard, where he always sat, and Rhea standing at the horses' heads with her slate on her belt. Anwen's bag was already up. Anwen was not. She was standing on the quay with her cap on, and her hair pinned under it, and her hands in her sleeves. And Kiva and Prue and Jude and Perrin stood round her, because that was how they stood. I've a thing for you, said Kiva.
